newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-RECORD CROWD PREDICTED FOR AUSTRALIA-NZ.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-RECORD CROWD PREDICTED FOR AUSTRALIA-NZ.

text.p: Australia will play New Zealand in July in front of the biggest crowd at a rugby union international for 22 years, the Australian Rugby Union (ARU) said on Wednesday.
The ARU has predicted a capacity crowd of 98,000 will fill the Melbourne Cricket Ground on July 26 to watch the traditional rivals face each other in a Tri-Nations clash.

"The combination of general public, member union, corporate and hospitality tickets sold already indicates we will have close to a record 100,000 watching," ARU managing director John O'Neill said in a statement.
ARU spokesman Greg Thomas said the latest batch of 26,000 tickets went on sale on Wednesday and all but 3,000 were sold on the day, guaranteeing a record crowd for a rugby union test in Australia.
It would be the biggest rugby union attendance in the world since a record 105,000 people watched the test match between Scotland and Wales in 1975, Thomas said.
In a break with previous practice, the ARU switched the match against the All Blacks to Melbourne, a city with no rugby union tradition, in a move aimed at increasing revenue from ticket sales.

The Melbourne Cricket Ground, which normally hosts cricket tests or Australian Rules football matches, has a capacity almost double that of any stadium in Sydney or Brisbane, the main centres of support for rugby union in Australia.
